guideTitle: Best Honeywell and Comparable Smart Dehumidifiers (2026)
metaDescription: Honeywell 30, 32 and 50 pint dehumidifiers compared with GE, Midea and Frigidaire on DOE capacity, pump drainage, Wi-Fi control and efficiency.
expertTake: The Honeywell TP-Fit 50 pint with a built-in pump is the best overall pick for a damp basement, because its capacity, pump and efficiency certification fit the real problem. The 32 pint Honeywell with Wi-Fi is the best smart choice for a medium room. The GE 50 pint is the value pick if you have a floor drain. Skip every machine here if the room has standing water, since you need to fix the source first.
introParagraphs: A dehumidifier's capacity number used to be easy to read, and then the test changed. In 2019 the government moved the standard to a cooler, more realistic condition, and the same machine suddenly rated about a third lower. Brands still sell under both scales, which is why two boxes with different pint labels can hold the same hardware.

This guide explains how to compare capacity, drainage and smart features across brands, and why efficiency certification matters on a machine that runs for months. Start with the picks above for the short list, then read the reviews below to match a unit to your room, your drain and your Wi-Fi.

specList.label: Drainage

products.description:
The TPFIT50PWK is the Honeywell to buy for a real basement. A 50 pint class machine with a built-in pump and a rated 4,000 sq ft reach sits a full size above the 30 pint and 32 pint Honeywell models, and the pump removes the one chore that makes a basement unit annoying: emptying the bucket. The pump can move water vertically or horizontally up to about 15 ft, so a utility sink, a floor drain or a window all work.

Two modes make it more than a bigger tank. Laundry mode keeps the machine running until damp clothes are dry, and Auto-Comfort mode adjusts operation based on room temperature, which suits a space that swings between seasons. Energy Star Most Efficient certification means it uses less electricity per liter of water removed than a standard certified unit, which matters because a basement machine can run for months. Compared with the GE 50 pint, it adds a pump and the two modes, while the GE has a bigger 15 pint bucket and no pump.

The same unit appears under two Amazon listings with the same TPFIT50PWK model code, so treat them as one product rather than two options. Keep the pump hose clear of kinks and flush it with diluted vinegar occasionally, since lint and algae can clog it. The washable dust filter, detachable tank and anti-spill splash guard cover routine upkeep. Thermal overload protection shuts the machine down if it overheats, which is a useful guard for a motor that runs for days at a time.
products.bestFor: A large or damp basement where a pump drain and Energy Star Most Efficient running costs matter.
pros: Built-in pump moves water up to 15 ft to a sink or window
Energy Star Most Efficient certification for lower running costs
Laundry and Auto-Comfort modes add useful programs
Thermal overload protection guards a motor that runs for days
cons: The same model is listed twice, which can confuse comparison
Larger and louder than the 30 pint and 32 pint Honeywell units
Pump hose and reservoir need flushing every few months

products.description:
The TP50AWKNR is the most instructive Honeywell, because its listing says outright that the machine removes 32 pints and was previously labeled 50 pints. Nothing about the hardware changed. In 2019 the DOE moved the test from 80F and 60% to 65F and 60% humidity, and the same compressor suddenly rates about a third lower. Seeing the old and new numbers in one place is the best demonstration of why you should compare DOE pints and ignore everything else.

It is a smart dehumidifier in the useful sense. Wi-Fi with Alexa and Google Home voice control lets you read and change humidity from upstairs, and a digital humidistat, a 24 hour timer, sleep mode and low temperature operation cover regular running. Energy Star Most Efficient status for 2023 is a real efficiency credit. Against the TP-Fit 50 pint model, it gives you a smaller machine with no pump but a larger apps and voice package, and it is a better fit for a medium room than a large basement.

Treat the 3,000 sq ft claim as a best case, since a 32 DOE pint unit is a mid-size machine. A detachable tank with anti-spill guards and a continuous drain tube cover the water handling. If your room is wet enough to fill the tank in a day, use the drain tube or step up to the pump model.
products.bestFor: A medium basement or living area where app and voice control and Most Efficient certification matter.
pros: Lists a 32 pint rating and notes the old 50 pint label, so it is honest
Wi-Fi, Alexa and Google Home voice control from anywhere
2023 Energy Star Most Efficient certification for low running costs
Continuous drain tube and anti-spill tank guards are included
cons: No built-in pump, so the drain tube needs a lower drain
The 3,000 sq ft claim is generous for a 32 pint machine
Smart features rely on the Honeywell app and a stable signal

products.description:
The 30 pint Honeywell is the smaller sibling of the TP50AWKNR and is a better fit for an apartment, a bedroom or a basement room than a whole level. It lists 30 pints in 24 hours for rooms up to 3,000 sq ft, though in practice it behaves like a small to medium dehumidifier. An LED display shows temperature, humidity and timer settings, so you can read the room at a glance without opening an app.

Alexa compatibility and two fan speeds give it a modest smart feature set. The anti-spill 7 pint tank is small compared with the larger machines, so continuous draining through the included tube and cap is the sensible way to run it in a damp space. Against the Midea 50 pint it is a smaller and lighter machine, and against the GE 50 pint it holds far less water, but it keeps Honeywell's full alert set: a water level indicator, full tank light, audible alarm and a clean filter reminder.

Ownership is routine. Wash the dust filter when the alert appears, wipe the tank and keep a few inches clear around the air outlet. Auto shutoff and auto restart cover full tanks and power cuts. If the 7 pint bucket fills more than once a day, move to the 50 pint models rather than emptying it constantly.
products.bestFor: A bedroom, apartment or small basement room that wants alerts and Alexa in a compact machine.
pros: Clean filter alert and full tank alarm reduce guesswork
LED shows room temperature and humidity at a glance
Alexa support and two fan speeds make it easy to control
A continuous drain tube and cap are included in the box
cons: The 7 pint tank is small, so continuous drainage is almost required
Capacity is far less than the 50 pint models for a wet room
Coverage claim of 3,000 sq ft is optimistic for 30 pints

products.description:
The GE 50 pint is the best comparison for the TP-Fit Honeywell, because it targets the same large room with a different design. It rates 50 pints a day for spaces up to 5,000 sq ft and has a large 15 pint bucket, which is about twice the size of the Honeywell 30 pint tank. Smart Dry adjusts fan speed based on room humidity, so the machine does not run flat out when the room is only slightly damp.

The big difference is the drain. GE says plainly that this product does not have a pump, so continuous drainage depends on a hose connection and a drain lower than the machine. That is why it is a value pick for a basement with a floor drain and a poor one for a basement where water must be lifted. A 10 second alarm warns you when the bucket is full or missing, a clean filter notice reminds you of upkeep and a 30% to 70% humidity setpoint range gives room to adjust.

As a larger compressor unit it is heavier and louder than the compact models, but the easy-roll wheels and pocket handles make it manageable. The hose is not included, so buy a standard garden hose to run it continuously. Wash the filter when notified and keep the coil clean. If you want Wi-Fi control, look to the Midea, since this listing does not mention app support.
products.bestFor: A basement with a floor drain where a large bucket and a simple 50 pint machine are enough.
pros: Large 15 pint bucket lasts much longer than the Honeywell tank
Smart Dry fan control avoids running flat out in a mild room
Humidity setpoint range of 30% to 70% suits most rooms
An alarm sounds when the bucket is full or has been removed
cons: No pump, so continuous drainage needs a lower drain
Drain hose is not included, so you must buy one separately
No Wi-Fi or app control is mentioned in the listing

specList.label: Connectivity

products.description:
The Midea 50 pint is the Honeywell TP-Fit's most direct rival in a Wi-Fi package. It rates 50 pints a day, covers up to 4,500 sq ft and lists 49 dBA at low speed, which is a reasonable noise figure for a unit this large. A cloud connected SmartHome app and Alexa and Google Assistant control let you manage it from anywhere.

The 35% to 85% setpoint range is wider than the 30% to 70% on the GE, which helps if you want to dry a space well below normal or hold a high humidity for a cellar. Compared with the TP-Fit, there is no pump in this version, though a separate Midea listing offers one, so check which you are buying. A drain connection takes a standard hose, but the hose is not included, so continuous drainage is a small extra purchase.

Rotating wheels and handles help you move a heavy unit. Because it is a Wi-Fi unit, make sure your router reaches the basement before you buy, otherwise the smart features will be dead weight. Rinse the filter regularly and place it with space on both sides. It is a good middle option if you want a 50 pint unit with Energy Star certification and app control but do not need a pump.
products.bestFor: A large basement with a floor drain and a strong Wi-Fi signal where you want an app.

Energy Star certified, which helps keep running costs down
cons: The listed model has no pump; the pump version is separate
Drain hose is not included, so you must buy one separately

products.description:
The Frigidaire 50 pint is the well-known appliance brand option in this comparison. The listing is short on numbers, which is the main caution: it states a 50 pint capacity, Wi-Fi, a washable filter and custom humidity control, but gives no coverage figure, noise rating or drain details beyond the broad category. That makes it harder to compare than the Honeywell or Midea listings, which give fuller specs.

What you are buying is a portable compressor machine from a brand with wide service coverage. Frigidaire markets it for a bedroom, living room, garage, attic or crawl space, which suggests the machine is intended to be moved between spaces. Against the Honeywell TP-Fit, you lose the stated pump, laundry mode and Most Efficient certification from the listing. Against the GE 50 pint, you gain Wi-Fi.

Check the full product page before buying for the drain method, the bucket size and the DOE rating. Ask whether a hose is included and whether the unit has an Energy Star mark. Clean the washable filter often and treat the humidity setting as a target to confirm with a separate hygrometer. If you need a specific drain solution, one of the better documented models above is a safer choice.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prefer a familiar appliance brand and want Wi-Fi control in a 50 pint machine.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Compare capacity on the new DOE scale
buyingCriteria.explanation: Since 2019 the DOE rates capacity at 65F and 60% humidity, replacing the older 80F test. A machine once sold as 50 pints is now commonly rated around 32 to 35 pints with identical hardware. The Honeywell TP50AWKNR listing says outright that it removes 32 pints and was previously labeled 50 pints, while the TP-Fit, GE and Midea models list 50 pints on the new scale. When two models list different pint numbers, check which scale each uses before deciding that one is bigger.

The most common reason a dehumidifier fails to do its job is a full bucket. Pump drainage, like the TP-Fit's 15 ft pump, moves water to a sink or window without a lower drain. Gravity hoses on the GE and Midea models need a floor drain, and the Honeywell 30 pint's 7 pint tank fills quickly. Walk the room first and note where the nearest drain is and how high it sits, then choose accordingly.

Energy Star Most Efficient is a higher bar than standard Energy Star and applies to units that remove more liters of water per kilowatt-hour. Both the TP-Fit and the TP50AWKNR carry it, while the 30 pint Honeywell and the Midea carry standard certification. On a machine that may run most of the year in a basement, the efficiency difference accumulates, so it is worth paying for if the room is damp for months.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Consider smart features for out-of-sight units
buyingCriteria.explanation: App and voice control are useful if the machine sits in a basement you rarely visit, because you can check the humidity and change the setpoint from upstairs. The Honeywell 32 pint, the Honeywell 30 pint, the Midea and the Frigidaire have Wi-Fi or Alexa support. The GE and the TP-Fit rely on onboard controls. Confirm the Wi-Fi signal reaches the basement first, since a weak signal makes the app useless.

If you will empty the bucket by hand, the size matters. The GE's 15 pint bucket lasts about twice as long as the Honeywell 30 pint's 7 pint tank before it fills. Alerts matter too: the GE sounds a 10 second alarm for a full or missing bucket and the Honeywell 30 pint adds a clean filter alert. A machine that stops silently with a full bucket will not keep a basement dry.

Refrigerant dehumidifiers frost their coil in cool rooms and must pause to defrost, which lowers output below 65F and nearly stops it below 41F. Honeywell lists low temperature operation, and most of the others list auto defrost, which protects the coil but does not restore capacity. A basement that stays at 55F needs a larger machine than the capacity chart suggests, such as one of the 50 pint models.

specDecoder.meaning: The DOE rates how much water a machine removes in 24 hours at 65F and 60% humidity. It replaced an older, warmer test in 2019, so identical machines now carry lower labels. It is the only figure that compares brands fairly.
specDecoder.watchFor: The old 50 pint label is the same hardware as the new 32 pint label on the Honeywell TP50AWKNR. If one listing says 50 and another says 32, check the test year.

specDecoder.meaning: This designation marks units that beat standard Energy Star efficiency, measured in liters of water removed per kilowatt-hour. A Most Efficient unit uses less electricity for the same water. It matters most for a machine that runs for months.
specDecoder.watchFor: The year matters, since criteria tighten. The Honeywell TP50AWKNR lists 2023 certification, so confirm the model code rather than trusting a brand claim.

specDecoder.meaning: A built-in pump pushes water through a tube, and the maximum vertical lift and length determine where you can drain. The TP-Fit lists a drain up to about 15 ft. Gravity drainage depends on the machine sitting above the drain.
specDecoder.watchFor: Pump hoses clog with lint and algae and can kink. Check the actual hose length in the box and plan the route before buying.

specDecoder.meaning: Coverage is a manufacturer estimate for a moderately damp open space. It ignores ceiling height, wet walls and doors. It is a rough guide to relative size, not a promise.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 30 pint Honeywell claims 3,000 sq ft, the same as the 32 pint model, so use pints and room wetness for sizing instead.

specDecoder.meaning: The setpoint range is the range of targets you can choose, not the range the machine can reach. The GE offers 30% to 70% and the Midea 35% to 85%. The machine cycles the compressor to hold the target.
specDecoder.watchFor: A wide range does not mean a larger capacity, and the built-in sensor can read a few points off. Confirm with a separate hygrometer.

howWeEvaluated.title: DOE capacity on one scale
howWeEvaluated.description: We converted the listings to one scale by favoring DOE style figures and the 2019 update, and noted old label changes. The Honeywell TP50AWKNR, relabeled from 50 pints to 32, is the clearest example. We ranked the 50 pint units above the 30 and 32 pint units on moisture removal.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pump, gravity and manual options. The TP-Fit's 15 ft pump ranked highest, the GE and Midea rely on hoses with no pump in the listed versions, and the Honeywell 30 pint has the smallest bucket. We also noted where the hose was not included.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency and certification
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed Energy Star and Energy Star Most Efficient claims. The TP-Fit and TP50AWKNR carry Most Efficient status, the Midea and Honeywell 30 pint carry standard certification and the GE and Frigidaire listings are less specific. We weighted this for machines that run most of the year.

howWeEvaluated.title: Smart and alert features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared Wi-Fi, voice control and alerts. The Honeywell 32 pint and 30 pint, the Midea and the Frigidaire have app or voice control, and the Honeywell 30 pint has the broadest set of alerts including clean filter. We gave smart features weight only for units that sit out of sight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked how much real detail each listing gave, including noise, coverage and drain information. The Frigidaire listing was the thinnest, while Honeywell and Midea gave fuller specs. A model with sparse detail dropped in rank despite a good brand.

howToChoose.intro: A pump lifts water, while gravity relies on a lower drain.

cards.label: Pump
cards.text: A pump moves water vertically and horizontally, so you can send it to a utility sink or out a window. The Honeywell TP-Fit with a built-in pump up to about 15 ft is the lineup example, and it suits basements where the drain is above the machine.

cards.label: Gravity
cards.text: A gravity hose needs a drain lower than the machine. The GE 50 Pint, the Midea 50 Pint, the Honeywell 32 Pint and the Honeywell 30 Pint rely on a hose or tank. These are simpler and have no pump to clog, but they need a floor drain.

howToChoose.note: Pick the pump model if the nearest drain is higher than the dehumidifier. Pick gravity if you have a floor drain and want fewer moving parts.

howToChoose.intro: Smart features are useful only when you will actually use them.

rows: App control on a larger unit
Alexa and a full alert set

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A basement needs real DOE capacity, a way to drain without carrying water and a machine that tolerates cool air. Look for a 50 pint class rating, a pump or a floor drain connection and low temperature operation. Efficiency certification matters because the unit may run for months.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Honeywell TP-Fit 50 Pint with Pump is the best basement pick because it combines 50 pints, a 15 ft pump and Most Efficient status. The GE 50 Pint is a fine choice with a floor drain, and the Midea 50 Pint adds Wi-Fi.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if the basement is large, damp for months or the drain is above the floor. The Honeywell TP-Fit with a pump and Most Efficient certification pays back in convenience and electricity over a long season.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if the room is a bedroom or a lightly damp space. The Honeywell 30 Pint or the GE 50 Pint covers it, and a pump or Most Efficient certification would be extra you do not use.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter cuts airflow and capacity. Rinse and dry before reinstalling.
Standing water grows film and odor. Wash with mild soap and dry.

maintenance.task: Flush the pump and drain line
maintenance.why: Lint and algae can block the pump. Run diluted vinegar and keep the hose sloped.
Dust on the coil lowers efficiency. Use a soft brush with the unit unplugged.
Smart units can lose their connection after a router change. Reconnect and test an alert.
Water left inside can stagnate. Drain, dry and store upright.

faq.q: Why does the same Honeywell show 32 pints in one listing and 50 pints in another?
faq.a: The DOE changed the test condition in 2019, from a warm room to 65F and 60% humidity. The same hardware that was rated 50 pints under the old test is now rated about 32 pints. The Honeywell TP50AWKNR listing mentions both numbers. Always compare units on the same scale.

Only if the drain is higher than the machine or far away. A pump, like the one in the Honeywell TP-Fit, lifts water through a hose to a sink or window. If you have a floor drain nearby, a gravity hose is simpler and has fewer parts to clean.

faq.q: Is Energy Star Most Efficient worth it?
faq.a: If the machine runs for months in a damp basement, yes. Most Efficient units use less electricity per liter of water removed than standard certified units, and the saving accumulates across a season. For a seasonal bedroom unit, standard certification is enough.

faq.q: How big a dehumidifier do I need for a basement?
faq.a: For a damp basement, a 50 pint class unit is a common starting point, especially if the space is larger than about 1,500 sq ft. Coverage claims are generous, so size by DOE pints and how wet the room is. If it runs nonstop and never reaches the target, you need a larger unit or a source fix.

faq.q: Do smart dehumidifiers need a good Wi-Fi signal?
faq.a: Yes. The app and voice control only work when the machine stays connected. Test the signal in the basement first, and keep the router firmware current. If the signal is weak, a basic model with a timer is the more reliable choice.

faq.q: What humidity should I aim for?
faq.a: Most guidance suggests keeping indoor humidity between 30% and 50%, with about 50% as a practical upper limit in summer. Mold becomes more likely when humidity stays above 60%. Use a separate hygrometer to check the reading, since built-in sensors can be a few points off.
